name: blast-unevacuated-casualties
description: The punishment path for issue #557: drill, charge a pattern, then fire WITHOUT ever running `zone clear` — the staffed driller/blaster crew and the drill_rig they drove out on are left standing exactly where their own work left them. Deterministic on seed 42: the crew dies with a bystander driver, two vehicles are destroyed, and the incident record shows it. This is the cost the tutorial's evacuate-zone step (and blastCommand's tutorial-mode refusal) exist to prevent.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:2 cols:2 spacing:3 depth:8 diameter:0.089 start:20,20
steps.description: 3x3 grid at the grid tool's own default spacing (DEFAULT_SPACING_M=3) — the (20,20)-(23,23) drag needs no spacing-stepper click first. #947 CI-fix: `diameter:0.089` added to match Drill.ts's DEFAULT_DIAMETER_M — the grid tool has no diameter stepper, so interaction mode always confirms at the UI's fixed 89mm regardless of clicks, while this command previously fell back to drillPlan.ts's own 0.15 default; that gap fed computeDrillHoleDurationTicks a different diameter per mode (same class of bug as blast-charge-loading-ui.json's #947 fix). Depth also diverged: the grid tool's own DEFAULT_DEPTH_M is 6m, not this command's declared 8m, and nothing below clicked the depth stepper to raise it — so interaction mode drilled shallower/faster holes than command mode simulated. Two increment clicks on the depth stepper (data-field="depth", default 6 -> 8) raise interaction mode's grid depth to match the command's own explicit depth:8 before the drag+confirm, instead of watering the scenario's declared depth down to the UI default. Rally-point spawns: the pattern starts at (20,20), not (15,15). The staffed crew now gathers around the rally flag at (2,8), which put the idle driver at (7,12) about 8.5m from a (15,15) pattern and inside its flyrock (a third death). At (20,20) the bystanders stand about 15m or more from the nearest hole, as they did before the rally flag existed, so only the crew that worked the pattern is caught.
#553/#590: drain the ordered drill plan — sandbox-measured landing well inside 300 ticks for the staffed roster's lone driller/drill_rig on this 9-hole grid.

Deliberately under-stemmed (0.5m on 8m holes): each hole fills with 7.5m of boomite (15kg at 2kg/m) — the reckless overcharge this file is built around, matching the flyrock-danger integration suite's own reckless config.
#554/#1649: drain the charge orders. A charging truck loads one hole at a time, so the budget is generous relative to the old on-foot pace.

#1673: weather follows the biome now (#1688) and the crew's shift rests move the timeline, so this desert site is not reliably rained on before the pattern is fired. Rain is set explicitly so the holes are wet for the tubing/drain steps below, whatever the clock reads.
Let the rain wet the drilled holes.

#1649: a charging truck loads one hole at a time, so the pattern stands long enough for weather to wet it, and a wet boomite charge fizzles instead of firing. The blaster buys tubing from the Charge step's tubing card (a real control) to make the holes drainable.

Install tubing in the holes: tubing does not remove water already in a hole but makes it drainable (porous untubed holes cannot be drained). The Install button tubes every untubed hole in one click, so in interaction mode the first install step does all four and the later ones find nothing left to click.
Tube hole H2 (already done by the single Install click in interaction mode).
Tube hole H3 (already done by the single Install click in interaction mode).
Tube hole H4 (already done by the single Install click in interaction mode).
Drain the now-tubed wet holes right before firing so the boomite charges fire instead of fizzling. Cost: HOLE_DRAIN_COST_PER_HOLE each.

No `zone clear` anywhere in this file — the crew that drilled and charged this pattern is left standing exactly where its own work left it, and so is the drill_rig it drove out on. This is what the evacuate-zone tutorial step and blastCommand's tutorial-mode refusal exist to prevent (#557).

expect.note: Deterministic on seed 42: the driller and blaster who charged this pattern die where they stood (#1, #2 at 20,22), and the drill_rig they drove out on and a second vehicle are destroyed. Fill-mode re-pin 2 -> 3: holes now fill to the 0.5m stemming (15kg each, the old pin loaded 8kg), so flyrock (fragment 151, ~3.4kJ) also kills the bystander driver Gus Pickaxe (#3) at (7,12), about 15m from the pattern. Nobody was evacuated — that's the whole point of this file.
